scenario: An ecologist is studying a small mammal population in a nature reserve. Camera traps have a weight-activated trigger that only fires for animals heavier than 5 kg, so lighter animals are never recorded. The ecologist uses the camera-trap records to report the average body mass of the species.

question: Camera trap records show a mean weight of 8.0 kg. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean body mass Î¼ of the full population (including animals below the detection threshold), and (b) the fraction of the population that is detected by the camera traps.
naive_answer: The true mean body mass is approximately 8.0 kg since that is the trap record average.
naive_trap: About 32% of the population is below 5 kg and invisible to the traps. The true mean is 6.4 kg â€” 1.6 kg lower than the trap average. An ecologist reporting 8 kg as typical body mass would systematically overstate the species' size, affecting habitat and resource models.

python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(5-mu)/3; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+3*norm.pdf(a)/sf-8 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,5.01,7.99)
assert abs(mu-6.443)<0.15
assert abs(norm.sf((5-mu)/3)-0.6848)<0.01
